What does rising US power demand mean for gas supply?
US power demand is entering a period of significant change. Data centres and other large loads are adding electricity demand, while the need for firm capacity and faster access to power is supporting renewed interest in gas-fired generation, including behind-the-meter projects. 
But planning for new gas-fired generation requires more than understanding where electricity demand will grow. Utilities also need to consider whether sufficient gas supply will be available, whether pipeline infrastructure can deliver it to the right locations, how LNG exports and other sources of demand could compete for supply, and what those dynamics could mean for regional gas prices.
What should utilities watch as gas and power markets become more interconnected?
Our new ebook, 'Can gas supply keep pace with rising US power demand?', explores five questions utilities and power-market participants should consider:

Where is new power-sector gas demand emerging? See why the location of new gas-fired and behind-the-meter generation matters alongside headline demand growth. 
Is gas supply growing in the right places? Explore why national production forecasts alone may not reveal whether sufficient supply will reach individual demand centres. 
Is pipeline investment keeping pace with demand? Understand why project location, capacity, timing and likelihood of development matter for future gas availability.
How much gas demand will LNG exports create? Examine how growing LNG exports could compete with domestic power generation for regional gas supply and infrastructure. 
What could these changes mean for regional gas prices? Learn why regional price forecasts, basis relationships, infrastructure and supply-demand conditions can provide important context for generation economics. 

How can utilities connect their gas and power market outlooks?
For teams already using Wood Mackenzie's Lens Power & Renewables solution, gas-market intelligence provides another layer to the power-market outlook. Lens Gas & LNG adds visibility into regional gas supply and demand, pipeline infrastructure and flows, LNG exports, pricing and supply economics. Together, these perspectives can help utilities assess power demand, generation requirements and the underlying fuel market as one connected picture.
